brands.d: Chennai silk-sari house founded by Nalli Chinnasamy Chetti, among the oldest sari shops in India, with stores across India, the USA and Singapore.
Chennai Kanjivaram sari brand founded by Ahalya S, curating handwoven Kanchipuram silks in boutique collections.
Niche handloom label founded by designer Sanjay Garg, known for reworked Chanderi and Banarasi weaves in a distinctive pared-back aesthetic.
Tata/Titan ethnic-wear brand launched in 2017 selling pure-fabric saris, dress materials and kurtas, with Weavershala weaver centres.
Mumbai sari brand founded in 2016 by sisters Sujata and Taniya Biswas, built on handloom cotton saris and a large weaver network.
Kolkata couture label of Sabyasachi Mukherjee, selling under the Sabyasachi name since 1999 and dominant in Indian bridal wear.
Mumbai couturier and film costume designer whose eponymous label is a leading Bollywood-linked bridal and occasion-wear house.
Mumbai designer behind House of Anita Dongre, spanning bridal couture and contemporary ethnic wear.
Jodhpur-born, Parsons-trained designer who launched his first label in 1994 and later Raghavendra Rathore Jodhpur, credited with globalising the Jodhpuri bandhgala.
Vedant Fashions' mass-premium Indian wedding and festive menswear chain, trading since 1999 with hundreds of stores and sister brands Mohey and Twamev.
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail's premium men's occasion and ceremonial ethnic-wear label, run through Indivinity Clothing Retail.
Pakistani clothing retailer founded by Shamoon Sultan in 1998, grown from handwoven khaddar into a lawn and ready-to-wear chain with stores abroad.
Karachi textile group incorporated in 1953, retailing fabrics and clothing through Ideas by Gul Ahmed.
Karachi label of Sana Hashwani and Safinaz Muneer, founded 1989, which built its name in unstitched seasonal lawn before expanding to ready-to-wear.

notes: Sari: old flat list (14 names) deduped into 16 regional-weave archetypes (each backed by a tradition entry); 'Toub (lafaya)' dropped here because it belongs to the African dress shelf (Toub kind); 'Kashmiri jamawar sari' kept in m with no retrieved source. Shalwar kameez: ao dai, baju kurung, baju Melayu and puletasi stripped (separate kinds on the Southeast Asian & Pacific shelf); kurta pyjama folded into types. Kurta: dashiki, barong tagalog, vyshyvanka and huipil stripped (own kinds on African, Southeast Asian and Americas shelves); Pathani suit moved to Shalwar kameez as an archetype; Bhopali, Hyderabadi, Sindhi, Punjabi and cowl kurtas kept as types. New kinds: Sari blouse & petticoat (sourced from the Choli article) and Bandhgala & Nehru jacket (Jodhpuri article). Brands: Tasva founding year and Tarun Tahiliani link not confirmed on the retrieved page so left blank; Manish Malhotra and Anita Dongre founding years not on retrieved pages so left blank; Mohey appears in Lehenga m as a Manyavar line. Fabindia, Biba, W and other mass ethnic-wear chains not added because no page was retrieved this session. The wiki tool failed with a lock error throughout, so all Wikipedia pages were retrieved via web_fetch (search → fetch); a sources log was kept in the sandbox.
